question.text: Six positive numbers are in GP, such that their product is 1000 . If the fourth term is 1 , then the last term is

solution.text:
Let the six terms of GP are
$$
\frac{a}{r^{5}} \cdot \frac{a}{r^{3}}, \frac{a}{r}, a r, a r^{3}, a r^{5}
$$
Now, according to the question $\frac{a}{r^{5}} \cdot \frac{a}{r^{3}} \cdot \frac{a}{r} \cdot a r \cdot a r^{3} \cdot a r^{5}=1000$
$\Rightarrow \quad a^{6}=(10)^{3} \Rightarrow a^{2}=10$
Also, given fourth term $=a r=1$
$\Rightarrow \quad a^{2} r^{2}=1$
$\Rightarrow \quad r^{2}=\frac{1}{10} \quad \ldots$ (ii)
$\therefore$ Last term $=a r^{5}=\left[a^{2}\left(r^{2}\right)^{5}\right]^{1 / 2}$
$=\left[10 \times \frac{1}{10^{5}}\right]^{1 / 2}[$ from Eqs. (1) and $(i i)]$
$=\left(\frac{1}{10^{4}}\right)^{1 / 2}=\frac{1}{100}$
